races.name: Twilight Racing Summer Series Maiden (Div I)
Twilight Racing Summer Series Maiden (Div II)
Conference & Banqueting Facilities @ Limerick Handicap

runners_data.name: Halon Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner dropping back from 8f-10f trips to a sharper 7f where his early pace becomes an asset rather than a liability; recent win at the trip on Good suits, but the STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder he is not a natural front-runner by profile — trainer Ciaran Murphy has a 2/14 14-day record to note, and 40 days off is manageable.

runners_data.name: Dawn Romance
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has winning form over 6f on Good ground, but all five recent runs have come at 5f-6f — this 7f trip looks a stamina question; hold-up style from rear needs a strong pace that may not materialise here, and the trainer's 0/5 14-day stat offers no encouragement.

runners_data.name: Zenford
runners_data.note: Consistent 7f performer with three placed efforts at the trip on Good to Soft and similar conditions, handling this ground profile comfortably; Ben Coen is a high-quality booking and a prominent racing style suits the likely race shape well — the absence of a win is the only caveat.

runners_data.name: Substance
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good and has placed at 7f, so the trip holds no fears; wears a tongue-tie, trainer JP O'Brien is firing with 11/68 in 14 days, and racing prominently from a handy position makes Substance structurally well-suited to the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Watch Tower
runners_data.note: 191 days off the track is a significant fitness flag for a lightly-raced 2-year-old, and all form to date came over 6f-7f on Standard (AW) and Good — first run on a softer surface is an unknown; prominent style suits the race shape but the layoff must temper confidence significantly.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Runs in a hood and has shown modest recent form — a six at 10f last time suggests she may be better-suited going shorter, and her 7f form shows a seventh; listed as unknown style (U), making her tactical role hard to pin down, and the trainer's 2/16 14-day stat is moderate at best.

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: Back just seven days after her last run, and nine runs without a win on Good or Soft tells the story — a hold-up horse who has placed at 7f-8f on soft-ish ground but consistently finds one or two too good; the short turnaround and uninspiring sim-going record (0W across nine runs) are both concerns.

runners_data.name: Fortuity
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good ground and placed over 8f, so the form profile is genuinely there; though mapped to midfield due to overcrowding of prominent types up front, she is a true prominent racer in nature — Keithen Kennedy (5lb claim) helps the weight, and trainer Mrs Harrington has 4/35 in 14 days; most likely of the displaced pair to recover some natural ground.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Returned seven days ago and that quick turnaround follows a series of mid-to-rear finishes at 6f-8f on Good ground — sim-going record of 0W across ten runs is poor; genuinely wants to race prominently but is squeezed out of that berth in this field, and without a win to his name at any level the profile is hard to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Trained by Noel Meade with Seamie Heffernan — a top pairing — and wears a hood; form figures of 864-59 are uninspiring at face value but the 39-day break could signal freshening, and an unknown tactical style (U) adds unpredictability; previous 4th over 6f on Tapeta and 5th over 8f on Heavy show she handles variation but the Good to Yielding surface record (3/5 runs) is the best context to use.

races.paceDynamic: Halon Bay is the confirmed lone pace-setter and will control the tempo from the front, with no genuine rival willing or able to challenge for the lead in the early stages — a sustainable, uncontested gallop is the near-certain outcome over this 7f on Good to Yielding ground. Behind him, Zenford, Substance, and Watch Tower are all prominent types who will track in behind the leader, creating a well-organised midfield queue rather than a scrappy, messy race. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Fortuity and Coincidental Glory are genuine prominent-minded horses but are mapped to midfield as Halon Bay, Zenford, and Substance are better-placed to hold the early slots; Fortuity is the more likely of the two to edge closer if the pace is genuinely honest. This race shape — a single controlled pace-setter, moderate ground, and a compact midfield — strongly favours horses who travel prominently just off the leader or can pick up powerfully from a handy position when the tempo is honest but not blistering, meaning prominent-to-midfield types with proven form at 7f on soft-ish ground hold the clearest structural advantage.

scenarios.title: Halon Bay Controls, Chasers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Halon Bay sets a sustainable, uncontested pace and the prominent chasers Zenford and Substance track close enough to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Halon Bay sets a sustainable, uncontested pace and the prominent chasers Zenford and Substance track close enough to pounce inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Leader Victorious
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace set by Halon Bay on soft-ish ground suits a galloping front-runner who is never challenged and simply idles home.
scenarios.body: If the moderate pace set by Halon Bay on soft-ish ground suits a galloping front-runner who is never challenged and simply idles home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Outstay Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses fail to make up ground on the yielding surface in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is honest enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses fail to make up ground on the yielding surface in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are slower than anticipated and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish that suits anything with residual speed from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the early fractions are slower than anticipated and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish that suits anything with residual speed from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tower has been off the track for 191 days — if G M Lyons has not freshened this filly sufficiently, she could drop out of contention early and leave the prominent pitch more congested than expected behind Halon Bay.

Fortuity and Coincidental Glory are both genuine prominent types forced into a midfield role by the field's composition — if either breaks sharply and claims a better early position than mapped, the tactical picture up front could become more contested than anticipated.

Dawn Romance's visor and the step up from 5f-6f to 7f on Going to Yielding ground is a significant combination of unknowns — if she is unable to settle from the rear, rider Jamie Powell may find her in no-man's land between hold-up and midfield.

The Good to Yielding ground is consistent across the Limerick card — no rail movement or going change is flagged for this race specifically, so the surface should be predictable, slightly testing but not deep enough to massively bias against any particular style.

races.name: Ballyduane Stud Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Spanish Temptress
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this field, giving her a structurally advantaged position; Richard John O'Brien's yard is 0/3 in the last 14 days but she returns on just 8 days' rest with solid recent form and a strong record on similar going (3 wins, 7 places from 15 similar-ground starts) — the race is hers to lose from the front.

runners_data.name: Fratas
runners_data.note: Back after 346 days off (324 days for jockey Sheridan), which is an enormous fitness concern regardless of her strong placed record on Good ground; she has class on the form book and a natural prominent style that suits the expected race shape, but the layoff must be respected heavily.

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator whose Good To Yielding figures (12 from 15 starts) are solid, but Sheila Lavery's yard is 0/6 over 14 days and Robbie Colgan will need a strong pace to set up her late effort — this slow-burn shape does her few favours.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on Good over three starts ago and clearly has ability; her true running style is hold-up, squeezed to midfield on this map because the field is stacked with rear-end types — Gabriella Hill (7lb claimer) will need to position her early to have any chance and Adrian McGuinness's yard is firing (1/28 over 14 days, modest strike rate).

runners_data.name: Thru And Thru
runners_data.note: Has a useful record in soft-ground conditions (6 from 7 similar-going runs placed) and Seamie Heffernan is an upgrade in the saddle; a genuine hold-up type over her best trip, she wants a stronger pace than Spanish Temptress is likely to set, but the soft-ground form edge is real.

runners_data.name: Una Matata
runners_data.note: Form on this surface is limited (1 from 15 similar-going starts), which is a concern on the Good To Yielding; she races prominently and is likely to slot in behind Spanish Temptress, giving her an honest position, but the going profile is a genuine flag.

runners_data.name: Tofino
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's yard is in solid form (7/64 over 14 days); his true style is prominent but he has been mapped to midfield given the traffic ahead of him — Robert Whearty will have to ride aggressively early if he is to get the position the horse needs, which may cost him later on the testing ground.

runners_data.name: Amemri
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has won on Standard and Good going but only 6 from 15 starts on similar ground to today; David Marnane's yard is active (4/17 over 14 days) and the horse is capable, but as a genuine hold-up type forced into midfield, he needs a pace scenario that simply may not materialise here.

races.paceDynamic: Spanish Temptress is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner fillies' handicap and, with no genuine rival willing or able to match her early, she should slide into an uncontested lead and dictate her own comfortable fractions over Limerick's flat mile. Fratas and Una Matata are the likeliest horses to track her from a prominent position, though Fratas returns from a 346-day absence and her fitness is a significant question mark. The Good To Yielding surface will blunt any sustained sprint finish, placing a premium on position and the ability to conserve energy behind a controlled pace rather than finishing with a fierce late kick. This race shape — a single, unhurried leader setting a sustainable tempo — emphatically favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and produce a measured, progressive effort in the straight rather than those who need a strong gallop to set up a late run. The field contains more prominent and hold-up types than can physically occupy their natural positions: Tofino, Gloriously Glam, and Amemri are all redistributed from their true roles, with Spanish Temptress and Fratas most likely to actually control the early stages while the others are forced to compromise their preferred patterns.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Temptress Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Spanish Temptress leads from the gate and faces no meaningful early pressure, settling into a rhythm that saps the finishing kick of those held up.
scenarios.body: If Spanish Temptress leads from the gate and faces no meaningful early pressure, settling into a rhythm that saps the finishing kick of those held up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Trade Blows
scenarios.trigger: If Fratas recovers from her long absence quickly and Una Matata pushes forward to challenge Spanish Temptress, creating a genuine two-way battle for the lead.
scenarios.body: If Fratas recovers from her long absence quickly and Una Matata pushes forward to challenge Spanish Temptress, creating a genuine two-way battle for the lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a horse comfortable sitting mid-division finds open ground on the flat Limerick straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses late and a horse comfortable sitting mid-division finds open ground on the flat Limerick straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Overcomes
scenarios.trigger: If one of Gloriously Glam, Tofino, or Amemri manages to secure a better position than their redistributed map slot suggests and the pace is brisk enough to suit.
scenarios.body: If one of Gloriously Glam, Tofino, or Amemri manages to secure a better position than their redistributed map slot suggests and the pace is brisk enough to suit.

watchPoints.text: Spanish Temptress's jockey Keithen Kennedy (5lb claimer) must judge fractions carefully — if he goes too slow on the front end he risks leaving a comfortable target for anything tracking him, but the horse's natural gate speed makes her the controlling force regardless.

Fratas's 346-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race; watch how she moves to post and behaves in the early stages — if she shows any signs of rustiness, her prominent position becomes a liability rather than an asset.

Tofino and Gloriously Glam are both likely to find themselves shuffled back from their natural positions at the break; watch for congestion in the first two furlongs if either rider tries to force forward, which could compromise multiple runners mid-pack.

The Good To Yielding ground (confirmed for this race in the going report) will place extra emphasis on stamina over the final two furlongs — horses who are stoutly bred or have won on soft ground recently (Thru And Thru, Anvika) may be underestimated in the market.

Una Matata's going record (1 from 15 on similar surfaces) is a stark statistical outlier worth noting if she drifts in the market — her position map looks fine but the ground is a consistent weak point in her profile.

races.name: Greenmount Suite @ Limerick Handicap

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a recent win over this exact course and distance on Good ground; McDonogh booked, which is a positive, and her sim-going record is modest but the course form is the key angle here.

runners_data.name: Crosshaven
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose recent form string of 07-0 is poor, and the fades-in-finish flag compounds a sim-going record that shows no wins or places on comparable ground; limited appeal.

runners_data.name: Green Icon
runners_data.note: Off-the-pace horse returning quickly off a 9-day break for a yard with a busy book; fades-in-finish flag, a run of zeros in recent form, and nothing in the sim-going record to suggest improvement is imminent.

runners_data.name: Limbocall
runners_data.note: Style unknown, returning from 316 days off — the long absence is the dominant concern, and while the trainer has had two winners from ten recently, this is very much a fitness question mark on comeback.

runners_data.name: Starting Monday
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over ten furlongs on Soft recently; the drop to a flat Limerick mile in a handicap suits its natural front-end style, and the claimer Darragh O'Sullivan on board carries a weight allowance that is meaningful at the top of the market.

runners_data.name: Captain Ciano
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form over ten furlongs doesn't obviously suit this flat mile drop; the sim-going record is modest and the trainer has drawn a blank over the past eight runners over the period.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: Off-the-pace mare who fades in the finish and has shown nothing in six recent attempts; sim-going figures are workmanlike but no wins or placed efforts on comparable conditions.

runners_data.name: Carvalhal
runners_data.note: Prominent type with four placed efforts from 15 on sim-going; the 5lb claim from Nicola Burns is meaningful, and a second-placed effort over 7f on Good is the form benchmark — stepping up to a mile should suit.

runners_data.name: Oitentinha
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse pushed forward on this pace map because the field is overloaded with rear-division types; the short-trip form (5f-7f) is the primary concern stepping into a flat mile, and the style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Darkness
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer whose best effort (a second) came over a flat mile on STA, but the fades-in-finish flag and a run of zeros recently undermine confidence; mapped to midfield rather than its natural position at the rear.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced hold-up type with only three career runs; its natural style places it further back than the map shows, and with just one good sim-going run from three, there is simply insufficient evidence to anchor confidence here.

runners_data.name: Saith Seren
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has been consistent without winning; five consecutive fifth-placed efforts suggest a hard-knocking type who finds one or two too good late — the redistribution into midfield may actually help it on this occasion.

runners_data.name: Liamo
runners_data.note: Off-the-pace horse whose one career win came on Good ground and whose trainer has had one winner from three recently; this is a flat mile step down from longer trips where it has raced recently, which is worth noting positively.

runners_data.name: Monroe Dasher
runners_data.note: Returning from 292 days off and placed into midfield rather than its natural hold-up berth; the absence dominates everything here, and four runs in the sim-going band produced no wins or places.

runners_data.name: Lady Crossing
runners_data.note: Returning from 140 days off, another hold-up type whose natural position could not be accommodated at the rear; fades-in-finish flag, poor recent form, and the absence make this a considerable risk at any price.

runners_data.name: Bright Image
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse who maps into midfield against its natural instincts; the headgear (tongue tie) is noted, and four placed efforts from ten on sim-going suggest it finds the frame without winning — quick turnaround after 7 days.

runners_data.name: Notforalongtime
runners_data.note: Recent runner who races genuinely off the pace but is slotted into midfield here due to the overcrowded rear; two placed efforts from seven on sim-going and a 9-day turnaround for Laura Hourigan's yard — the proximity to the leaders enforced by the field size may not suit its patient style.

runners_data.name: Friars Gate
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning quickly (9 days) with a fades-in-finish flag; four recent runs over this trip on Good have all resulted in mid-pack or worse finishes, and there is no obvious angle to suggest a reversal now.

runners_data.name: Racing Royalty
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this field and therefore controls the entire pace dynamic; its style-fit tag reflects a prominent horse operating at the limit of its role, but the uncontested lead on Good to Yielding for a yard currently without recent winners is the central tactical fact of this race.

races.paceDynamic: Racing Royalty is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no other confirmed lead horse to pressure it, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled gallop on Good to Yielding ground over this flat Limerick mile. Starting Monday and Carvalhal are the prominent types most likely to slot in just behind, sitting within a length or two of the leader and covering their position early. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up horses — Notforalongtime, Oitentinha, Saith Seren, Liamo, Monroe Dasher, Pure Valour, Heart Of Darkness, Lady Crossing and Bright Image are all genuine off-the-pace types who cannot all find their natural rearward berth in a 19-runner field and will be shuffled into a compressed midfield pack instead. With one front-runner setting an uncontested, measured tempo and Good to Yielding ground that rewards stamina and momentum, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or in the first third of midfield and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than true closers who need a strong gallop to generate the gaps they require.

scenarios.title: Royalty Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Racing Royalty leads at a controlled pace and the prominent horses behind never seriously challenge for the lead.
scenarios.body: If Racing Royalty leads at a controlled pace and the prominent horses behind never seriously challenge for the lead.

scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Starting Monday or Carvalhal improve into the straight from close-up positions and quicken past a tiring front-runner.
scenarios.body: If Starting Monday or Carvalhal improve into the straight from close-up positions and quicken past a tiring front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield manage to find clear runs and the early pace is fast enough to collapse the leaders.
scenarios.body: If the genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield manage to find clear runs and the early pace is fast enough to collapse the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Front-Runner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected runner hustles forward to challenge Racing Royalty early, injecting genuine pace and collapsing the front end.
scenarios.body: If an unexpected runner hustles forward to challenge Racing Royalty early, injecting genuine pace and collapsing the front end.

watchPoints.text: Racing Royalty's uncontested lead is the defining tactical reality — if it gets loose on a comfortable gallop, watch whether Starting Monday or Carvalhal have the gears to close the gap in the final two furlongs rather than simply tracking in vain.

The 19-runner field on a flat Limerick mile creates significant traffic risks at the top of the straight — horses like Notforalongtime and Saith Seren, squeezed into midfield against their natural hold-up style, may find their runs closed off at the crucial moment.

Starting Monday's recent win came over ten furlongs on Soft; if the pace is too slow for this flat mile trip and the race becomes a sprint from two out, its stamina-based profile may be exposed against quicker types like Carvalhal.
Limbocall (316 days off) and Monroe Dasher (292 days off) are both long-absentees who could need the run sharply — monitor their market moves before the off for any stable confidence signals.

Carvalhal's 5lb claim from Nicola Burns is a live weight advantage in a compressed handicap field where the OR ratings span only 20 points (OR 40–60); small weight differentials at this end of the handicap can swing margins significantly.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Martin Molony Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Chally Chute
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old front-runner with winning form over comparable trips on Good ground; Ross O'Sullivan's yard shows a solid 14-day strike rate, and Chally Chute is ideally placed as the lone pace-setter — his 229 days off the track is the one risk here.

runners_data.name: Cristal Clere
runners_data.note: Won over 8f at the Curragh on Heavy recently and has placed form at 13f on Good going; a true front-runner by inclination who will find horses ahead of him from the gate, making his position in this race harder to secure than it looks on paper.

runners_data.name: Leinster
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-racer for Joseph O'Brien who has five runs at this exact trip, winning once and placing twice more on Good ground — excellent course-trip-going fit and a jockey booking from the in-form O'Brien yard warrants respect.

runners_data.name: Arouet
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old with two wins and a placed effort over 10-18f on Good and Heavy; headgear (p) worn, naturally wants to race up with the pace but is likely to find Chally Chute and the established prominent types ahead of him — STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Happy Pharoah
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien-trained four-year-old with a win at 13f on Good and second at 14f on Good; tongue-tie fitted, proven at the trip and going, and races prominently in a way that suits the anticipated race shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Layfayette
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Noel Meade who won over 14f on Heavy at the Curragh recently and has placed at 16f on Good; headgear (p) worn, needs a stronger pace than Chally Chute is likely to set — tactical disadvantage in this shape.

runners_data.name: Sunchart
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, adding an unusual angle; hold-up stayer with placed form on Soft and Good over middle distances but 55 days since last run and a lack of front-rank form suggests he needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Uxmal
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old O'Brien runner with wins at 14f on Soft and 22f on Good; 229 days off the track is a significant fitness query but the stamina profile is exceptional — if fit, the step back from extreme distances to 1m4½f on Yielding could see him prominent and competitive.

runners_data.name: Goodie Two Shoes
runners_data.note: The most consistent performer in the field: five wins at 14-16f on Good and Soft ground, topspeed ratings to match, headgear (t) worn, and an O'Brien/McDonogh combination in fine form — 227 days since last run is the only caveat in an otherwise strong profile.

runners_data.name: Bubble Gum
runners_data.note: Genuinely front-running type by nature, trained by JP Murtagh, with a win over 12f on Good but running from a lower OR and having been beaten in recent starts at shorter trips — the redistribution to midfield reflects how crowded the prominent berths are, not his preference.

runners_data.name: That's Amore
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett runner with a win at 11f on Standard and a placed effort at 12f on Good; limited turf soft-ground form (0W0P on sim-going) and naturally wants to race prominently in a field already full of front-runners — faces a difficult positional battle before the race even starts.

runners_data.name: New Zealand
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old, youngest in the field, with a win at 7f on Good and placed efforts at 10-13f; headgear (p) worn, wants to race forward but is likely to be outpaced for position by older, stronger prominent types — the experience gap at Listed level is a genuine concern.

races.paceDynamic: Chally Chute is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field and, with no genuine pressure expected to materalise early, should be allowed to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 1m4½f at Limerick. Behind him, Leinster, Happy Pharoah, Goodie Two Shoes and Uxmal are legitimate prominent-tracked types who will compete for the seats directly behind the leader, while Layfayette and Sunchart will settle further back as genuine hold-up operators. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Cristal Clere, New Zealand, Arouet, Bubble Gum and That's Amore are all true prominent horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the slots are already filled, with Arouet and Cristal Clere most likely to actually push forward and challenge for a prominent berth. A single unhurried pace-setter in a slowly-run Listed race on soft-ish ground over this stamina trip strongly favours those who can sit close to the action and produce a sustained gallop home — the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile is the one to back here, not hold-up finishers who will find insufficient tempo to close off.

scenarios.title: Chally Chute Controls, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Chally Chute leads at a comfortable clip and the race is not disrupted from behind, allowing the prominent-position chasers to deliver their challenge approaching the straight.
scenarios.body: If Chally Chute leads at a comfortable clip and the race is not disrupted from behind, allowing the prominent-position chasers to deliver their challenge approaching the straight.

scenarios.body: If several of the redistributed prominent types — Arouet, Cristal Clere, New Zealand — push forward to contest early position, creating a faster-than-expected pace that stretches the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chally Chute Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and no challenger has the confidence to commit to a move until too late, leaving Chally Chute to steal the race on the bridle.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely slow and no challenger has the confidence to commit to a move until too late, leaving Chally Chute to steal the race on the bridle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from the outset to string the field out and the prominent horses are asked for effort too soon, leaving late-running opportunities for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from the outset to string the field out and the prominent horses are asked for effort too soon, leaving late-running opportunities for the hold-up horses.

watchPoints.text: Goodie Two Shoes and Happy Pharoah are both prominent-tracking types with strong trip-and-going form — if either secures a close position behind Chally Chute from the start, they are the most dangerous horses in the race.
Uxmal and Chally Chute both return from 229-day absences; watch the market moves for both in the hour before the race as confidence in their fitness will be reflected in price movement.

Arouet, Cristal Clere and New Zealand will all want to race prominently — monitor how aggressively they are ridden from the gate, as any three-way scrimmage for position behind Chally Chute could inject unexpected pace and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Layfayette is the most interesting hold-up horse if the pace quickens — Noel Meade's runner has recent winning form at the trip and going but relies on a tempo that this pace map suggests is unlikely to materialise organically.

New Zealand carries the lowest weight in the field at 124lbs and is trained by Aidan O'Brien who is in strong 14-day form (9/37); the age and weight allowance could offset the experience deficit if the race falls kindly positionally.

races.name: McMahons Builders Providers Maiden

runners_data.name: Faithful Follower
runners_data.note: High-class OR-120 seven-year-old with a win and three places in similar ground (sim-going 1W3P), the most credible threat here on form; a natural rear-runner by design but likely to travel closer than usual given the lack of true pace, and Seamie Heffernan's experience will be key in finding the right position — the 45-day absence is the only query.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old whose two runs on Good ground both ended in tail-finishes (11th and 12th), the fade-in-finish flag is backed by a sim-going record of 0W0P in three attempts; Emmet Mullins' 14-day record of 0/8 adds no confidence, and this horse has to find significant improvement to be involved.

runners_data.name: Wrob And Wryan
runners_data.note: Well-beaten in all recent starts including a 12th on Good ground, this hold-up type has been bumped forward on the map from its preferred rear position due to field composition — a true closer forced to race out of role in a race with minimal pace, and the form figures of 5005-0 offer no optimism at this level.

runners_data.name: An Cailleach
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with two runs, both well beaten on Soft going, and the headgear flag (p) suggests connections are searching for answers; the fade-in-finish warning and 0W0P sim-going record make this a difficult proposition, and being pushed toward midfield from a natural hold-up position does not help.

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and pace-setter, wearing a visor for K J Condon (1/3 in the 14-day window) with Ben Coen aboard — maps to prominent/lead and has the best recent form line with a 2nd on Good ground nine days ago; controls the race shape entirely and the uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage at this trip.

runners_data.name: Cascade Canyon
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a single mid-field placing (4th) in four runs for Kevin Coleman (1/8 in 14 days), a genuine hold-up horse repositioned to midfield by necessity; 1m4½f is an untested trip but the horse has run over 1m2f and upward, and a T14 of 1/8 does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Ravens Can Fly
runners_data.note: A three-year-old with just two runs, both on Good ground and both well beaten, trained by Slattery (1/27 in 14 days) with an apprentice in the saddle; the fade flag and 0W0P record suggest a horse still learning its trade rather than one ready to compete in a maiden at this level.

runners_data.name: Royal Sapphire
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien-trained three-year-old (T14: 9/56 — best strike rate in this field) with Declan McDonogh, who is a significant booking; headgear (b) applied and the horse has a 7th as its best, but the fade flag and 0W0P in eight sim-going starts are concerning — O'Brien volume means this may be more of a run for experience.

runners_data.name: Second Line
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's three-year-old has posted consistent 8th-place finishes without threatening, and 38 days off the track adds uncertainty; a hold-up type whose fade flag is well-documented, and the 1m4½f step up from shorter trips is unproven — no sim-going wins or places in three attempts.

runners_data.name: Blissful Bonita
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's three-year-old (T14: 6/51) is listed as unknown style and has posted placings (5th, 6th, 7th, 5th) without winning in five starts; the form figures are more consistent than many here and the trip looks suitable stepping up from 8f, making this one of the more interesting unknowns in a weak field.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flagged ⚠ as such — just two runs, a 6th on Soft and 8th on Heavy, both at shorter trips; K J Condon (2/10 in 14 days) now steps her up to 1m4½f and the open style designation leaves genuine uncertainty about tactics, which could be a plus if the shape suits.

runners_data.name: Themis
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old (T14: 8/55) has posted a best of 7th and carries a strong fade warning; a genuine hold-up type forced to race closer than ideal given the map compression, and 0W0P in four sim-going runs offers little encouragement — a horse that needs pace to be made, which this field may not truly generate.

runners_data.name: Tintinabulla
runners_data.note: Ms Sheila Lavery's three-year-old with just two runs — an 8th and a 14th — and a fade-in-finish flag with 0W0P in both sim-going starts; James Ryan takes the ride but there is very little in the form to suggest a step forward is imminent over this 1m4½f trip.

races.paceDynamic: Taj Crown is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-horse field and, with no rival likely to dispute the lead, Ben Coen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m4½f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Limerick. The pace will be honest but not frantic — a single leader setting a measured tempo over a flat track creates a genuine sit-and-sprint dynamic in the straight, favouring horses who can travel close to the pace rather than those making up ground from deep. The field carries a significant concentration of hold-up horses — Faithful Follower, An Cailleach, Cascade Canyon, Wrob And Wryan, Themis and Royal Sapphire are all true rear-runners who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the race shape simply cannot accommodate that many closers, and in practice several will race closer than their style suggests; those most likely to actually secure prominent positions are Faithful Follower (higher class, experienced) and potentially Blissful Bonita or Mare Crisium given their unknown/flexible style profiles. The tactical verdict is clear: with one uncontested front-runner and a field packed with hold-up types forced closer than ideal, the race shape favours horses that can travel prominently or mid-division and produce a sustained run from 2f out — true closers relying on a strong pace to set up a late burst are at a structural disadvantage here.

watchPoints.text: Taj Crown (Ben Coen) is the only front-runner in a 13-horse field — watch whether he is allowed to stride clear unchallenged before the turn for home, as an uncontested lead on this flat track could prove decisive.

Faithful Follower is a natural rear-runner but the pace map shows he will need to settle closer than ideal — watch Seamie Heffernan's positioning in the first quarter-mile, as a poor start or tardy draw could leave him with too much to do against a front-runner who steals a march.

Royal Sapphire carries the Declan McDonogh/Joseph O'Brien combination (T14: 9/56) with blinkers applied — watch for any market move pre-race, as this barn runs large numbers but the booking is a notable upgrade and the application of headgear may signal a fresh approach.

Several hold-up horses — including An Cailleach, Themis and Cascade Canyon — will be racing in tighter quarters than their natural style demands; watch for traffic trouble and interference in mid-division on the turn, which is a live risk when multiple closers are compressed into the same section of the field.

Blissful Bonita and Mare Crisium carry the most stylistic uncertainty (both listed Unknown) — watch how each is ridden in the first half-mile, as either travelling prominently early would immediately elevate their chance given the lack of competition for those positions behind Taj Crown.

races.name: Racing Again On 2nd July Handicap

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride for Richard O'Brien and this 5yo has placed at this trip before; similar going form is sparse (1 place from 5) and a 47-day absence adds a question mark, but he is likely to be one of the genuine pace-setters in the absence of Omniscient.

runners_data.name: Satono Chevalier
runners_data.note: The headgear note (p) and two recent wins — one over 13f on good — suggest he arrives in good form for Flannery; similar-going record is thin (3 from 15) but the 18-day turnaround is positive, and as a natural prominent type he is well-placed to exploit a breakaway if rivals scramble for position.

runners_data.name: Slurricane
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's horse ran just seven days ago and is a confirmed prominent racer, but his similar-going record is poor (11 from 15 going average) and recent form strings show a slide in finishing position; will press early but his tendency to fade is a concern.

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who comes with a flagged "fades in finish" warning; similar-going form is middling (5 from 7) and a four-race run of double-digit finishes on good-ish ground makes it hard to be enthusiastic despite the extra stamina test.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: Flannery's horse has won over 12f on standard at the Curragh and has solid recent form (4-1-1-9-0); naturally races prominently — here he is pushed back into midfield by the density of pace in this field — which works against his chance and his 0.93 style-fit score should temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Dawn Coming
runners_data.note: A four-timer of placed efforts over long distances including third at 17f on good and 17f soft, Dawn Coming has genuine staying credentials; however, after 243 days off (92 days since last jockey ride) and being a natural front-runner squeezed into a midfield role by the pace dynamic, recency and position combine as dual concerns.

runners_data.name: Palace Rock
runners_data.note: Off the track for 819 days (509 since last jockey ride), Palace Rock's form trail is distant and best form came at longer distances; he is a natural prominent racer who cannot get that berth here, and the combination of layoff length and style displacement makes confidence very low.

runners_data.name: Chemdawg
runners_data.note: Has won over 19f and placed over 20–22f on soft, so stamina is his genuine asset; the tb headgear and a 235-day absence (22 days since last jockey ride) are noted, and while he would naturally press forward, this crowded pace map forces him back — his stayers' profile means he may be less harmed by that than some.

runners_data.name: Eben Zaabeel
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan rides for A J Martin but this 5yo has posted three consecutive zeros (10th, 11th, 14th) and his best placed effort came 2nd at 11f on standard; headgear (t) in place, 19-day turnaround is fine, but the form trajectory is discouraging.

runners_data.name: Battle Of Maldon
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 3yo is the joint-top OR in the race at 82 and has a recent win over 10f soft to his name; Declan McDonogh rides and the prominent style (p headgear) means he should find a position without needing to force it, making him one of the more interesting profiles with improving form.

runners_data.name: Mighty Wave
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's 3yo wears a b and carries the least weight (119lbs); only three runs in the book with a third over 8f soft and fifth over 12f good, so stamina for this trip is unproven — a hold-up horse who would need the pace to be strong and genuine to get involved late.

runners_data.name: Omniscient
runners_data.note: Non-runner — Gordon Elliott's horse was the only confirmed front-runner in the field; his absence removes the single reliable pace anchor and is the pivotal factor shaping every scenario in this race.

races.paceDynamic: With Omniscient now a non-runner, the confirmed front-runner is absent and the race loses its single pace anchor, leaving Quatre Bras, Satono Chevalier, and Slurricane as the most likely pace-setters from the prominent brigade. The going is Good to Yielding throughout the card at Limerick — a shade softer than the declared Good to Soft — which will stretch the 1m4½f trip and reward stamina over speed. This field is packed with natural prominent types: Genoah, Dawn Coming, Palace Rock, and Chemdawg are all genuine front-runners or prominent racers who cannot all hold their preferred positions and will be pushed into a midfield role they are unlikely to relish, inflating early fractions without those horses benefitting from doing so. The race shape favours a well-positioned, genuine prominent racer or a resolute hold-up horse with proven stamina on soft-ish ground who can pick through the likely mid-race traffic, with a genuinely contested early pace on this ground tipping the balance toward closers with stamina rather than speed.

watchPoints.text: Pace scramble at the start — with Genoah, Dawn Coming, Palace Rock, Chemdawg, Quatre Bras, and Satono Chevalier all wanting to race prominently, the first two furlongs could be hectic; any runner caught in traffic or checked early faces a compromised chance over this stamina-heavy trip on yielding ground.

Dawn Coming's layoff (243 days, 92 since last jockey ride) is significant — if her trainer has her fit enough she has the stayers' profile to be competitive, but race-fitness must be questioned and she is worth monitoring in the betting market for confidence signals.
Palace Rock's absence of 819 days makes her an extreme each-way risk; if punted into shorter prices, be aware that no meaningful recent racecourse evidence exists for the current ground or trip.

Battle Of Maldon is the youngest horse in the field (3yo) at the joint-highest OR (82) and has an upward form curve — watch whether Declan McDonogh allows him to travel kindly in midfield rather than force the pace, as his profile suits a race run at a solid gallop on this ground.

The going report consistently reads Good to Yielding across all eight races at Limerick — marginally softer than the declared Good to Soft — and every race at 1m4½f has been run on this surface today; horses with proven form on genuinely soft or yielding ground hold a real advantage over those whose best form is on a faster surface.
